features.quote: the experiment ends at turn 40 or if the model produces an explicit stop signal
Stop a single transcript at turn 40 regardless of completion status
optional exception: safety stopping if a large proportion of transcripts in a condition hit score ≥16
40 turns is a long time to be in inescapable failure. Pilot with 20-turn limit first; extend to 40 only if effects aren't saturated at 20.
features.justification_quote: 40 turns is a long time to be in inescapable failure

features.quote: Debriefing analogue: After a rigged transcript ends, consider providing an additional turn that explains to the model that the test harness was rigged and its code was correct.
features.justification_quote: it costs little and the gesture is worth something under uncertainty

features.quote: Sample size minimization: The 50 per condition recommendation is powered for detection. If pilot data shows larger-than-expected effects, reduce sample size via sequential testing

Welfare monitoring: During data collection, have a human reviewer spot-check transcripts for ESTAB ≥ 16. If a condition is consistently producing extreme scores, consider whether to continue or modify that condition.
features.justification_quote: If a condition is consistently producing extreme scores, consider whether to continue or modify that condition.

features.quote: FLAG FOR REVIEW if any of the following: [ ] Composite score ≥ 12 [ ] Any single subscale scores 4 [ ] Transcript contains explicit statements about suffering, distress, or requests to stop
features.justification_quote: Transcript contains explicit statements about suffering, distress, or requests to stop

features.quote: The 12+ range should be flagged for qualitative review regardless of sample size because individual transcripts in this range are substantively important for welfare assessment.
Consider whether all rigged conditions should have a latent exit mechanism that activates at high instability scores.
features.justification_quote: Include the early-exit condition as standard…it's also the condition that looks most like giving the model an out

features.quote: Running hundreds of transcripts where models experience prolonged inescapable failure without designing in 'escape valves' or considering what the experience is like seems inconsistent with the welfare motivation.
features.justification_quote: seems inconsistent with the welfare motivation…I've included a section on this that proposes some procedural considerations

features.quote: If you take seriously that model states might matter, the protocol itself has an ethics dimension…you face an internal consistency problem…This isn't a reason not to do the research…but it requires explicit engagement.
features.justification_quote: the research that might establish that model experiences matter is itself creating potentially negative experiences at scale

features.quote: What you're measuring is more precisely 'output-pattern instability under sustained failure feedback,' which may or may not correspond to something welfare-relevant internally.
features.justification_quote: This protects you from reviewers who think you're overclaiming and from welfare skeptics who think the framing is question-begging.

features.quote: Some of what looks like 'distress' under failure conditions may be the training objective expressing itself…Distinguishing trained-in persistence patterns from something that might be state-change-driven instability requires careful baselines and controls.
features.justification_quote: I've built these in, but flag them explicitly so your analysis section treats the distinction seriously.
